## b9ada70e7181

**Reproduced teaching defect.** Checked generator SHA-256 `2763ce8d2f80aafd4cb43b10825b113d89abe191ef45b31595874fe74ffe779f`; the executed canonical rule hash was `ecef11380da5` and matched the catalog.

At medium difficulty, seed `222`, consecutive lesson start `36`, demonstrations use sample indices `[36, 37, 38]` and the query uses index `39`. The intended rule preserves top-to-bottom pebble order within each non-wall column and bottom-packs the sequence. The executable rival `reverse_per_column_stack_order` reverses each sequence before bottom-packing. It matches all three demonstrations because demo 36 has no multi-pebble stack, demo 37 has only palindromic stacks `[4,4]` and `[9,9]`, and demo 38 has palindromic stacks `[4,1,4]` and `[1,1]`. It differs on the query, which contains non-palindromic stacks `[4,3]`, `[4,1]`, and `[3,7]`.

All four inputs pass the generator's `self_check` and belong to its documented domain. The supported Racket apply command produced the retained authority outputs. All five canonical inputs have zero columns containing multiple pebbles, so the canonical examples also fail to identify within-column order. This is therefore a lesson-level ambiguity, not a bad label or out-of-domain attack.

Evidence: `checks/audit/b9ada70e7181/counterexample.json`, `checks/audit/b9ada70e7181/input.json`, and `checks/audit/b9ada70e7181/racket.json`. No audit-target source was modified.
